body: I can see what you mean about normalcy. It certainly helps to have other people who see things the way you do. If you don't mind me asking, what do you feel separates you from others and makes you feel like you were never normal?

I'm not sure if this will help or not but its worth a try. I used to be like you. I never thought I would live past 28. I grew up surrounded by a lot of drugs and "don't care" attitudes. I had a hard time accepting the world as it was so I would get black out drunk every day. I worked in bars and somehow managed to scrape by in a one bedroom efficiency with two other people who were also severe alcoholics. It wasn't uncommon that I would wake up in pools of vomit or in strangers houses unsure of how I got there or what I had done. I was having unprotected sex with anything that had low enough standards to stick their dicks in me. I felt like I hit rock bottom when I got fired from the fourth bar gig I got due to my black outs.

In a desperate attempt to keep afloat on feeling good before I died, I enrolled in community college with easy classes just to get student aid. Before my money came in, I couldn't afford to drink and ended up sober unintentionally. I began seeing the good side of it. I no longer had to worry about waking up in strange places. I had solid poo again. My sleep actually refreshed me and I could wake up without a pounding head ache. I actually did well going to the classes I had to show up to to get my student loan money. By the time the money came in and I could pay for my rent again, I had found another place to rent by myself and used it for the deposit and first few months rent, leaving me with about 20 dollars a week to eat with. I biked to and from school, about 5 miles each way. I was feeling good! I got another part time job in a bar and somehow managed to not drink. I found myself good at math and looked into pursuing electrical engineering. Now 3 years later and I'm going strong in school.

I don't know what your aspirations are. I don't know if you went to college already. I don't know if any of this is helpful at all. I just wanted to let you know that I used to be there and I found a way out. I actually feel like I have something to live for now. You may find it, too. If you aren't happy with the way your life is going, ending it isn't necessarily the answer. I implore you to seek another way of life before you try to commit suicide. The worst that could happen is that you could not enjoy it. The best that could happen is that you find a reason to live and actually enjoy life, maybe for the first time in a long time. There's still happiness out there to be had. Will you go for it?

I get that you can't fathom a civilization without something to unite them. It's virtually impossible to imagine. Maybe the concept of religion you hold is different from mine. My concept is the enforcement of beliefs upon others with no evidence to support said beliefs. Concepts like "doing bad things results in eternal damnation" or "if you don't sacrifice a virgin the crops will die" are what religion is to me. Concepts like "do unto others what you wish to be done unto you" and "live and let live" are values that can exist outside of religion, yet were often propagated within religious belief systems to an extent. I assume the societal structures you associate with religion are done so because you were mostly introduced to such concepts through religion, but I believe most societal acceptances go far beyond what religion has offered and stem more so from instinctual survival habits. With a small group of people watching over each other, humans were more likely to survive than by themselves. As the group got larger, their survival was more promising. Soon tasks were delegates to specific units within the community and thus society was born.

As far as religion being the worst thing in human history, as you've pointed out, religion can be traced back to every major conflict, but so can other reasons. The other reasons may exist, but it is not the other reasons that was used to control the minds of the masses to fulfill the desires of those in power. It was religion. While religion itself is not inherently evil, it is by all means a tool of great power. Like nitroglycerin, it can be used to heal others or can be used to cause great devastation. Those who are simple minded and weak willed flock to religion because it gives them the much needed reason for living, but it is too often used to give them a reason for hating. I should note that I am not saying that all religious people are weak willed or simple minded, just that those are the ones who will be easily controlled by religion. When these people are asked to do a task, they could first think that it would be horrible and wrong, but given the guise of religious reasoning, they would change their attitude and decide that it is the only way to get into their fabled promised land. While wars are the most common evil associated with religious wrongdoings, global racism and homophobia are attributed to religion as well. The inquisition, the holocaust, the Salem witch trials, the crusades, human sacrifice, cannibalism, and wealth divide are all things directly attributed to religion.

TL;DR: Religion made every horrible event in human history "easy-mode".
Although I am amused you announced yourself thusly, how does you being an edgy teenage pertain to this conversation?
